pairs.subject: module-design
pairs.evidence: app/_lib/request-body.ts:118 readJsonWithLimit hands any non-null parsed JSON to the caller as T. The doc comment's claim that every route validates its shape is only a convention: app/api/apply/[id]/route.ts:213 reads `body.answers` as Record<string, unknown> without a shape check. So the region is enclosed by convention rather than construction, while a verified alternative (returning `unknown`) costs almost nothing.

techniques.evidence: app/_lib/request-body.ts:118 The cast is described in the doc block, but enclosure depends on callers. The stated invariant is false for at least one caller, which falls under the technique's 'verified alternative exists' debt case. By contrast, api-response.ts:81-82 brands before it casts and states why.
app/_lib/rate-limit.ts:44 Time is passed in as a parameter instead of being read from a clock inside the limiter.
app/_lib/api-response.ts:52 The auth gate is injected, which keeps the pure response vocabulary free of the DB-backed auth layer.
app/_lib/request-body.ts:90 One deep helper owns the byte cap, the timeout and the parse for twenty routes. Its only defect is the type-assertion half covered above.
